label: Tientsin treaty-port blockade and coerced settlement of 1939

source_assertions.title: The Annotated Raphael's Mundane Astrology
source_assertions.claim: The 1939 Aries Ingress for London timed the Tienstin Incident, when Japan blockaded the British concessions on 14 June 1939 and Britain ended the blockade by handing over the four Chinese fugitives on 20 August 1939; the involvement of the Sun, Mars, and the 6th and 9th houses is evident in this international incident.

notes: Phase 5 seeded trade-and-commerce case for treaty-port blockade, foreign trade hostility, and coerced commercial settlement.

label: Britain heavy-taxation and restriction climate after 1947

source_assertions.title: Mundane Astrology: The Astrology of Nations and States
source_assertions.claim: Carter says the August 9, 1947 Saturn-Pluto conjunction, for Britain, may be read as the paralysing of business initiative by heavy taxation and the innumerable restrictions imposed by the Socialist government.

notes: Second-source trade-and-commerce case for commercial restriction and policy-driven paralysis rather than bank panic alone.

label: Suez Canal closure and shipping disruption, 1956-1957

source_assertions.title: Mundane Astrology: The Astrology of Nations and States
source_assertions.claim: Green assigns shipping, sea traffic, colonial trade, and commercial powers to the ninth house, making maritime-route interruption a valid trade-and-commerce output rather than a purely diplomatic one.

source_assertions.title: National Army Museum, Suez Crisis
source_assertions.claim: The National Army Museum's Suez crisis summary says Britain's oil supply was damaged by the canal's closure during the crisis and that the canal reopened to shipping in April 1957.

notes: Phase 5 expansion case for commercial and shipping interruption under canal closure rather than treaty-port coercion alone.

label: Oil-embargo trade and commercial disruption, 1973-1974

source_assertions.title: The Annotated Raphael's Mundane Astrology
source_assertions.claim: Raphael assigns foreign trade to the seventh house and shipping, colonial trade, commerce, and disputes in trade and commerce to the ninth, so embargo or route disruption belongs to trade-and-commerce logic as well as diplomacy.

source_assertions.title: Office of the Historian, Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969-1976, Volume XXXVI
source_assertions.claim: The State Department's historical preface treats the 1973-1974 oil embargo as a long-term energy-market shock with major consequences for consumers and allied economies.

notes: Phase 5 expansion case for embargo-driven trade and market disruption beyond shipping blockades and domestic restriction policy.

label: Smoot-Hawley tariff and protectionist trade contraction in 1930

source_assertions.title: Mundane Astrology: The Astrology of Nations and States
source_assertions.claim: Green ties commerce and trade to the second house and legislation affecting trade to eleventh-house parliamentary action, making protectionist tariff acts a valid trade-and-commerce outcome.

source_assertions.title: Britannica on the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act
source_assertions.claim: Britannica describes the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of June 17, 1930 as a protectionist law that raised tariffs and deepened trade contraction during the Depression.

notes: Post-Phase-5 hardening case for tariff-driven trade contraction outside the energy and shipping subfamily.

label: Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act liberalization in 1934

source_assertions.title: Mundane Astrology: The Astrology of Nations and States
source_assertions.claim: Green says benefic ninth-house and Sun-Jupiter trade testimonies can improve shipping, foreign trade, and commercial treaties, supporting liberalization as a valid trade-and-commerce output.

source_assertions.title: Office of the Historian on interwar protectionism and reciprocity
source_assertions.claim: The Office of the Historian identifies the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as the U.S. move away from Smoot-Hawley protectionism toward negotiated tariff reduction and expanded trade agreements.

notes: Post-Phase-5 hardening case for the positive side of trade-and-commerce, not only restriction and disruption.

label: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade signed in 1947

source_assertions.title: Mundane Astrology: The Astrology of Nations and States
source_assertions.claim: Green ties shipping, foreign trade, and commercial legislation or treaties to the ninth and eleventh houses, allowing multilateral trade agreements to be judged as trade-and-commerce events.

source_assertions.title: WTO chronology of the multilateral trading system
source_assertions.claim: The WTO chronology records the signing of the GATT on October 30, 1947 as the formal start of the postwar multilateral trading system.

notes: Post-Phase-5 hardening case for multilateral trade governance and commercial treaty structure.

label: Kennedy Round tariff-cut package in 1967

source_assertions.title: Mundane Astrology: The Astrology of Nations and States
source_assertions.claim: Green treats benefic trade legislation and commercial treaty conditions as distinct positive commerce outcomes, which supports tariff-cutting rounds and negotiated liberalization inside the trade domain.

source_assertions.title: WTO chronology of the multilateral trading system
source_assertions.claim: The WTO chronology identifies the 1964-1967 Kennedy Round as a major tariff-reduction negotiation package completed in 1967.

notes: Post-Phase-5 hardening case for a second multilateral liberalization event beyond the original GATT signature.
